bull_bear.body: Heavy reinvestment in capacity (Pune plant); Working capital optimization (NWC reduced to 18.7% of sales); No specific dividend/buyback commentary provided in transcript.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution risk on new Pune plant timeline; Intense competition in OEM segment pressuring pricing; Raw material volatility (Steel) and FX fluctuations; Dependency on intercompany transactions with SKF India Ltd during transition.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on volume growth and strategic repositioning; Transparent on margin headwinds being temporary (mix/one-offs); Pragmatic about competitive intensity; Focused on 'ACES' strategy (Acceleration of localization, Commercial excellence, Execution, One SKF).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Margin guidance of 15% by FY30 is conservative compared to historical 16-18% potential, explicitly due to strategic choice to regain market share in lower-margin OEM segments (Wind/Rail) rather than pruning them for profitability. The 'One SKF' strategy refers to internal functional alignment within the demerged industrial entity, not joint go-to-market with the automotive parent.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Affiliation with Sweden-based SKF Group (global engineering expertise combined with local manufacturing and channel transfers)
- Advancing localisation (~60% overall localisation level, ~78% local procurement in the year) reducing import dependence, lead times and supply-chain risk
- Technology-led differentiation via energy-efficient bearings, application-specific sealed solutions and magnetic bearing technologies
- Shift toward integrated lifecycle solutions (condition monitoring, lubrication, digital tools) with solution-led projects secured at margins upwards of 25%
- Quality systems framework (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, statistical process control, Six Sigma/TQM) supporting reliability in demanding industrial applications
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and supply chain disruptions — Shifts in global trade dynamics, tariffs and regional uncertainties may disrupt supply continuity and influence input costs; company response is strengthening localisation, diversifying sourcing channels and enhancing digital supply chain visibility.
- Currency fluctuation — A significant share of finished products are imported from other markets, creating higher currency fluctuation risk; the Company is offsetting this through increasing localisation and pricing actions.
- Manufacturing footprint and localisation execution risk — Delays in capacity expansion or localisation initiatives (including the Pune 'Factory of the Future') may affect growth plans, operational flexibility, export opportunities and the ability to scale industrial operations.
- Raw material, energy and logistics cost variability — Volatility in commodity, alloy, steel, energy and freight costs may influence margins and operational planning; margin pressure may persist despite pricing actions.
- Talent and capability risk — Limited availability of specialised engineering and digital talent may affect execution capability and constrain scaling of advanced capabilities.
- Information security and cyber risk — Increasing reliance on digital systems (MES, condition monitoring, digital procurement) heightens exposure to cybersecurity threats and evolving data protection requirements.
- Technology substitution and commoditisation risk — Alternative technologies, extended equipment life or customer insourcing may affect demand; intensifying competition from domestic and regional players with aggressive pricing/localisation in commoditised segments.
- Organisational transition post-demerger and exposure to cyclical capex-driven end markets — The Company must scale independent systems, governance and capabilities while maintaining customer continuity following the October 2025 demerger; demand is also linked to infrastructure, mining and metals capex cycles sensitive to project timing and policy execution.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: OEM mix increased to 50% (from 46%); Distribution decreased to 32% (from 38%). FY26 Full Year Mix: OEM 51%, Distribution 35%, Exports 6%, Sales to SKF India 4%. Key OEM verticals: Wind (7% of FY sales, +91% QoQ in Q4), Rail (11%), Metals (6%), Heavy Industry (7%), General Machinery (7%).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Frames itself as a Focused Industrial Company operating with agility as an industrial pureplay, with sharper capital allocation following the demerger from SKF India Limited.
- Positions to benefit from India's growth story, aiming to outgrow key segments such as Wind, Metals and Heavy industries.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] Financial information for the periods 17-Dec-2024 to 31-Mar-2025 and 1-Apr-2025 to 30-Sep-2025 was extracted by management from SKF India Limited's records for the demerged Industrial undertaking, prepared under Appendix C of Ind AS 103 (Business Combinations).
- [Key Win] Secured a Wind segment contract worth INR 140 Cr with a global gearbox OEM.
- [Key Win] Secured an Agri segment contract worth INR 35 Cr with a leading tractor OEM.
- [Macro] Cites India macro tailwinds — RBI FY27 GDP forecast of 6.7%, a rebound in industrial output, and India's position as the world's 4th largest wind capacity market growing +10% YoY — as demand context for Wind, Steel/Construction and core industries.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company manufactures and supplies bearings and units, seals, mechatronics and lubrication systems, together with allied lifecycle services, for industrial applications such as railways, mining, cement, metals, wind energy and general machinery. It was carved out via the demerger of SKF India Limited's Industrial business (effective 1 October 2025) and listed independently on the NSE and BSE on 5 December 2025, selling through OEM (51% of sales) and Distribution (35%) channels.

latest_quarter.body: Q4 normalized margin 11.5% (down from 13.1% Q3) due to higher OEM mix (lower margin than distribution) and full bonus accrual. Cost inflation projected at 3-4% (Steel, Oil, FX). Mitigation: Price hikes implemented in distribution; negotiations ongoing with OEMs. Royalty/trademark fees to parent increased expenses by ~INR 60M.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: ~8% CAGR until new plant commissioning; Margin: ~13% near-term (end-CY26), targeting 15% by FY29-30; Order Inflow: Strong traction in Wind (ZF, Suzlon) and Rail; Capex/Commissioning: INR 800Cr+ over FY26-FY30, new Pune plant commissioned by end-CY28.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not explicitly quantified as a backlog; however, significant order deliveries confirmed in Q4 for Wind (ZF, Suzlon) and Metals (Tata Steel, SAIL). Management highlighted winning a INR 32.5Cr tractor order and extended maintenance contracts for suburban trains.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Re-entry into previously exited low-margin segments (Wind, specific Rail freight, Agriculture) enabled by localization; Introduction of high-value products like hybrid ceramic bearings for data centers (currently imported); Expansion of tapered roller bearing SKUs locally.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deepen localisation further and strengthen supply-chain resilience to serve customers with greater reliability
- Accelerate the transition toward service-led and lifecycle-oriented revenue streams where margins and relationships are more durable
- Improve earnings quality through disciplined portfolio management and sustained operational excellence
- Improve margin profile through manufacturing and sourcing efficiencies, deepening localisation, pricing discipline and expanding sales of solutions
- Position as a provider of integrated lifecycle solutions by combining the product portfolio with engineering expertise, condition monitoring, lubrication and digital capabilities
- Pursue technology-led differentiation through energy-efficient bearings, application-specific sealed solutions, magnetic bearing technologies and digital tools (intelligent product selector, AI-enabled condition monitoring)
- Use demerger-enabled independence for clearer capital allocation toward highest-value industrial opportunities and faster, more agile decision-making
- The Company has adopted a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (as mandated under SEBI LODR Regulation 43A), publicly disclosed on the Company website, governing the framework for dividend declaration. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a final dividend of INR 10 per equity share, to be placed before shareholders for approval at the 2nd AGM, indicating an intent to share profits with shareholders as an independently listed entity.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is investing in a next-generation 'Factory of the Future' manufacturing facility in Pune, integrating manufacturing, solutions and supply-chain capabilities on a single scalable platform, structured to leverage channel transfers from within India and from SKF's global network to build capacity faster while maintaining capital discipline. During the year, advanced manufacturing channels were commissioned at the Pune factory for medium deep-groove ball bearings above 150 mm OD and UC-range ball bearing units, part of a plan to scale from 12 existing channels to 12 existing plus 8 new channels in the new factory. The Company currently operates a single manufacturing location supporting the Industrial segment, with Pune as the primary Industrial hub.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global industrial bearings market expected to grow from USD 54.6 Billion (2025) to USD 92.53 Billion by 2031 (9.2% CAGR 2026-2031), driven by electrification, automation and infrastructure investment
- Indian industrial bearings market estimated at ~INR 66,000 Crores (2024), projected to reach ~INR 97,000 Crores by 2033 (4.33% CAGR)
- Infrastructure-led demand from railway modernisation, freight corridors, metro networks, mining, cement and construction supporting bearing demand
- Record Union Budget 2026-27 allocation of INR 2,78,000 Crores to Indian Railways for network expansion, electrification, rolling stock and freight corridors expected to support demand for bearings and reliability solutions
- Renewable energy / wind capacity growth (record 6.05 GW wind addition in FY26 vs 4.15 GW prior year; installed wind capacity 56.09 GW as of March 2026) supporting demand for specialised high-load, corrosion-resistant bearings
- Capital goods sector growth with capacity utilisation improving to ~74-75%, supporting demand for plant, machinery and engineering equipment
- Industry shift toward aftermarket and service-led opportunities - condition monitoring, lubrication management, remanufacturing and asset reliability services alongside product sales
- Growing adoption of sensor-enabled bearings, condition monitoring and predictive maintenance (Industry 4.0 / smart manufacturing) increasing demand for precision, digitally connected bearing solutions
- Localisation and supply-chain realignment by manufacturers strengthening local production capabilities, supporting customised India-specific solutions
- Raw material, energy and freight cost volatility (alloy/steel prices) remains a risk to cost structures, requiring procurement resilience and pricing discipline
- Electrification / EV transition driving demand for specialised bearings, though impact seen as more pronounced in automotive-focused applications than broader industrial markets
- Margins for the year reflected one-time transition costs associated with the demerger; underlying operating performance described as stable, with structural earnings-quality improvement expected as transition costs normalise
- Near-term margins may moderate due to planned investment in the Pune manufacturing facility and digital capabilities, while laying foundation for long-term value creation

deepdive.thesis: SKF India (Industrial) delivered strong Q4FY26 sales growth (+9.8% QoQ) driven by a resurgence in Wind and Rail OEM segments, though reported margins were impacted by mix shift and residual demerger costs. The company is pivoting toward a 15% margin target by FY30 via aggressive localization and a new Pune plant, prioritizing market share recovery in previously exited segments over immediate margin maximization.

risks.note: Shifts in global trade dynamics, tariffs and regional uncertainties may disrupt supply continuity and influence input costs; company response is strengthening localisation, diversifying sourcing channels and enhancing digital supply chain visibility.

A significant share of finished products are imported from other markets, creating higher currency fluctuation risk; the Company is offsetting this through increasing localisation and pricing actions.

risks.risk: Manufacturing footprint and localisation execution risk
risks.note: Delays in capacity expansion or localisation initiatives (including the Pune 'Factory of the Future') may affect growth plans, operational flexibility, export opportunities and the ability to scale industrial operations.

risks.risk: Raw material, energy and logistics cost variability
risks.note: Volatility in commodity, alloy, steel, energy and freight costs may influence margins and operational planning; margin pressure may persist despite pricing actions.
Limited availability of specialised engineering and digital talent may affect execution capability and constrain scaling of advanced capabilities.
Increasing reliance on digital systems (MES, condition monitoring, digital procurement) heightens exposure to cybersecurity threats and evolving data protection requirements.

Alternative technologies, extended equipment life or customer insourcing may affect demand; intensifying competition from domestic and regional players with aggressive pricing/localisation in commoditised segments.

risks.risk: Organisational transition post-demerger and exposure to cyclical capex-driven end markets
risks.note: The Company must scale independent systems, governance and capabilities while maintaining customer continuity following the October 2025 demerger; demand is also linked to infrastructure, mining and metals capex cycles sensitive to project timing and policy execution.

one-line thesis: SKF India (Industrial) delivered strong Q4FY26 sales growth (+9.8% QoQ) driven by a resurgence in Wind and Rail OEM segments, though reported margins were impacted by mix shift and residual demerger costs. The company is pivoting toward a 15% margin target by FY30 via aggressive localization and a new Pune plant, prioritizing market share recovery in previously exited segments over immediate margin maximization.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 9.5B (+9.8% QoQ, +31% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 9.5% reported (11.5% normalized ex-demerger costs, down from 13.1% Q3 normalized due to mix); PAT: Not explicitly broken out, PBT at 9.5% (11.5% normalized); Order Book: Not disclosed (Project-based OEM flows); Net Debt: Not disclosed - One-offs: INR 183M demerger IT costs in Q4 (vs INR 1.8B in Q3 including stamp duty).
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~8% CAGR until new plant commissioning; Margin: ~13% near-term (end-CY26), targeting 15% by FY29-30; Order Inflow: Strong traction in Wind (ZF, Suzlon) and Rail; Capex/Commissioning: INR 800Cr+ over FY26-FY30, new Pune plant commissioned by end-CY28.
order book & pipeline: Not explicitly quantified as a backlog; however, significant order deliveries confirmed in Q4 for Wind (ZF, Suzlon) and Metals (Tata Steel, SAIL). Management highlighted winning a INR 32.5Cr tractor order and extended maintenance contracts for suburban trains.
segment / subsidiary detail: OEM mix increased to 50% (from 46%); Distribution decreased to 32% (from 38%). FY26 Full Year Mix: OEM 51%, Distribution 35%, Exports 6%, Sales to SKF India 4%. Key OEM verticals: Wind (7% of FY sales, +91% QoQ in Q4), Rail (11%), Metals (6%), Heavy Industry (7%), General Machinery (7%).
growth verticals / optionality: Re-entry into previously exited low-margin segments (Wind, specific Rail freight, Agriculture) enabled by localization; Introduction of high-value products like hybrid ceramic bearings for data centers (currently imported); Expansion of tapered roller bearing SKUs locally.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 normalized margin 11.5% (down from 13.1% Q3) due to higher OEM mix (lower margin than distribution) and full bonus accrual. Cost inflation projected at 3-4% (Steel, Oil, FX). Mitigation: Price hikes implemented in distribution; negotiations ongoing with OEMs. Royalty/trademark fees to parent increased expenses by ~INR 60M.
capex / expansion: Total plan INR 800Cr+ (FY26-FY30). Primary driver: New greenfield plant in Pune (DGBB and TRB channels) to be commissioned by end-CY28. Interim capacity managed via job work from SKF India Ltd and optimization of existing lines (e.g., Pune TRB capacity raised from 600k to 886k units with 18% cost reduction).
capital allocation: Heavy reinvestment in capacity (Pune plant); Working capital optimization (NWC reduced to 18.7% of sales); No specific dividend/buyback commentary provided in transcript.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on new Pune plant timeline; Intense competition in OEM segment pressuring pricing; Raw material volatility (Steel) and FX fluctuations; Dependency on intercompany transactions with SKF India Ltd during transition.
management quality / tone: Confident on volume growth and strategic repositioning; Transparent on margin headwinds being temporary (mix/one-offs); Pragmatic about competitive intensity; Focused on 'ACES' strategy (Acceleration of localization, Commercial excellence, Execution, One SKF).
non-obvious takeaways: Margin guidance of 15% by FY30 is conservative compared to historical 16-18% potential, explicitly due to strategic choice to regain market share in lower-margin OEM segments (Wind/Rail) rather than pruning them for profitability. The 'One SKF' strategy refers to internal functional alignment within the demerged industrial entity, not joint go-to-market with the automotive parent.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: SKF India (Industrial) Limited, an affiliate of Sweden-based SKF Group, manufactures and supplies bearings and engineered industrial solutions across India, following its demerger from SKF India Limited and independent listing in FY2025-26.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and supplies bearings and units, seals, mechatronics and lubrication systems, together with allied lifecycle services, for industrial applications such as railways, mining, cement, metals, wind energy and general machinery. It was carved out via the demerger of SKF India Limited's Industrial business (effective 1 October 2025) and listed independently on the NSE and BSE on 5 December 2025, selling through OEM (51% of sales) and Distribution (35%) channels.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- SKF India Limited — related party: Former parent; demerged company from which the Industrial business was carved out via NCLT-sanctioned Scheme of Arrangement (effective 1 October 2025). Interim Transition Service Arrangements (ISA) exist for sharing of common facilities and functions between the two entities, cross-charged with mark-up.
- SKF GmbH, Schweinfurt, Germany — related party: Fellow subsidiary and SKF Group company; subject of a shareholder resolution at the 2nd AGM to approve material related-party transactions.
- Tenute SRL — related party: Fellow SKF Group entity named in related-party disclosures.
- Peer Bearing Company-Changshan — related party: Fellow SKF Group entity named in related-party disclosures.
- Ningbo General Bearing Co Ltd — related party: Fellow SKF Group entity named in related-party disclosures.
- SKF Svéd Golyóscsapágy Zrt. (Sap) — related party: Fellow SKF Group entity named in related-party disclosures.
- SKF Automotive Belgium III NV — related party: Fellow SKF Group entity named in related-party disclosures.
- SKF Automotive USA INC. — related party: Fellow SKF Group entity named in related-party disclosures.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: OEM mix increased to 50% (from 46%); Distribution decreased to 32% (from 38%). FY26 Full Year Mix: OEM 51%, Distribution 35%, Exports 6%, Sales to SKF India 4%. Key OEM verticals: Wind (7% of FY sales, +91% QoQ in Q4), Rail (11%), Metals (6%), Heavy Industry (7%), General Machinery (7%).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **Industrial:** Bearings and units, Seals, Mechatronics, Lubrication systems, Condition monitoring and lifecycle services, Remanufacturing / oil recovery (RecondOil)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Railways
- Metals
- Mining
- Cement
- Wind / renewable energy
- General machinery / industrial automation
- Construction
- India (primary market)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not explicitly quantified as a backlog; however, significant order deliveries confirmed in Q4 for Wind (ZF, Suzlon) and Metals (Tata Steel, SAIL). Management highlighted winning a INR 32.5Cr tractor order and extended maintenance contracts for suburban trains.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: ~8% CAGR until new plant commissioning; Margin: ~13% near-term (end-CY26), targeting 15% by FY29-30; Order Inflow: Strong traction in Wind (ZF, Suzlon) and Rail; Capex/Commissioning: INR 800Cr+ over FY26-FY30, new Pune plant commissioned by end-CY28.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Re-entry into previously exited low-margin segments (Wind, specific Rail freight, Agriculture) enabled by localization; Introduction of high-value products like hybrid ceramic bearings for data centers (currently imported); Expansion of tapered roller bearing SKUs locally.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global industrial bearings market expected to grow from USD 54.6 Billion (2025) to USD 92.53 Billion by 2031 (9.2% CAGR 2026-2031), driven by electrification, automation and infrastructure investment
- Indian industrial bearings market estimated at ~INR 66,000 Crores (2024), projected to reach ~INR 97,000 Crores by 2033 (4.33% CAGR)
- Infrastructure-led demand from railway modernisation, freight corridors, metro networks, mining, cement and construction supporting bearing demand
- Record Union Budget 2026-27 allocation of INR 2,78,000 Crores to Indian Railways for network expansion, electrification, rolling stock and freight corridors expected to support demand for bearings and reliability solutions
- Renewable energy / wind capacity growth (record 6.05 GW wind addition in FY26 vs 4.15 GW prior year; installed wind capacity 56.09 GW as of March 2026) supporting demand for specialised high-load, corrosion-resistant bearings
- Capital goods sector growth with capacity utilisation improving to ~74-75%, supporting demand for plant, machinery and engineering equipment
- Industry shift toward aftermarket and service-led opportunities - condition monitoring, lubrication management, remanufacturing and asset reliability services alongside product sales
- Growing adoption of sensor-enabled bearings, condition monitoring and predictive maintenance (Industry 4.0 / smart manufacturing) increasing demand for precision, digitally connected bearing solutions
- Localisation and supply-chain realignment by manufacturers strengthening local production capabilities, supporting customised India-specific solutions
- Raw material, energy and freight cost volatility (alloy/steel prices) remains a risk to cost structures, requiring procurement resilience and pricing discipline
- Electrification / EV transition driving demand for specialised bearings, though impact seen as more pronounced in automotive-focused applications than broader industrial markets
- Margins for the year reflected one-time transition costs associated with the demerger; underlying operating performance described as stable, with structural earnings-quality improvement expected as transition costs normalise
- Near-term margins may moderate due to planned investment in the Pune manufacturing facility and digital capabilities, while laying foundation for long-term value creation

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 normalized margin 11.5% (down from 13.1% Q3) due to higher OEM mix (lower margin than distribution) and full bonus accrual. Cost inflation projected at 3-4% (Steel, Oil, FX). Mitigation: Price hikes implemented in distribution; negotiations ongoing with OEMs. Royalty/trademark fees to parent increased expenses by ~INR 60M.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Heavy reinvestment in capacity (Pune plant); Working capital optimization (NWC reduced to 18.7% of sales); No specific dividend/buyback commentary provided in transcript.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is investing in a next-generation 'Factory of the Future' manufacturing facility in Pune, integrating manufacturing, solutions and supply-chain capabilities on a single scalable platform, structured to leverage channel transfers from within India and from SKF's global network to build capacity faster while maintaining capital discipline. During the year, advanced manufacturing channels were commissioned at the Pune factory for medium deep-groove ball bearings above 150 mm OD and UC-range ball bearing units, part of a plan to scale from 12 existing channels to 12 existing plus 8 new channels in the new factory. The Company currently operates a single manufacturing location supporting the Industrial segment, with Pune as the primary Industrial hub.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on volume growth and strategic repositioning; Transparent on margin headwinds being temporary (mix/one-offs); Pragmatic about competitive intensity; Focused on 'ACES' strategy (Acceleration of localization, Commercial excellence, Execution, One SKF).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Affiliation with Sweden-based SKF Group (global engineering expertise combined with local manufacturing and channel transfers)
- Advancing localisation (~60% overall localisation level, ~78% local procurement in the year) reducing import dependence, lead times and supply-chain risk
- Technology-led differentiation via energy-efficient bearings, application-specific sealed solutions and magnetic bearing technologies
- Shift toward integrated lifecycle solutions (condition monitoring, lubrication, digital tools) with solution-led projects secured at margins upwards of 25%
- Quality systems framework (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, statistical process control, Six Sigma/TQM) supporting reliability in demanding industrial applications

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk on new Pune plant timeline; Intense competition in OEM segment pressuring pricing; Raw material volatility (Steel) and FX fluctuations; Dependency on intercompany transactions with SKF India Ltd during transition.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Margin guidance of 15% by FY30 is conservative compared to historical 16-18% potential, explicitly due to strategic choice to regain market share in lower-margin OEM segments (Wind/Rail) rather than pruning them for profitability. The 'One SKF' strategy refers to internal functional alignment within the demerged industrial entity, not joint go-to-market with the automotive parent.

strategy.body:

- Accelerate the transition toward service-led and lifecycle-oriented revenue streams where margins and relationships are more durable
- Improve earnings quality through disciplined portfolio management and sustained operational excellence

other.body:

- [Key Win] Secured an Agri segment contract worth INR 35 Cr with a leading tractor OEM.
- [Macro] Cites India macro tailwinds — RBI FY27 GDP forecast of 6.7%, a rebound in industrial output, and India's position as the world's 4th largest wind capacity market growing +10% YoY — as demand context for Wind, Steel/Construction and core industries.
